title: Galatians Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Galatians chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Galatians Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Galatians Chapter 2.

questions.question: In Galatians 2, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Paul went up to Jerusalem with Barnabas
Titus was compelled to be circumcised
The gospel of the uncircumcision was committed to Paul
questions.correctAnswer: Paul went up to Jerusalem with Barnabas
questions.explanation: This event is mentioned first in Galatians 2:1.

questions.question: Who accompanied Paul when he went up to Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Barnabas is mentioned as accompanying Paul in Galatians 2:1.

questions.question: What was the reason Paul went up to Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Paul states in Galatians 2:2 that he went up by revelation.

questions.question: Who was not compelled to be circumcised?
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:3 explicitly mentions that Titus was not compelled to be circumcised.

questions.question: What did false brethren attempt to do?
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:4 states that false brethren came in privily to spy out our liberty.

questions.question: How long did Paul give place to false brethren by subjection?
questions.explanation: According to Galatians 2:5, Paul did not give place by subjection for even one hour.

questions.question: What was the purpose of not giving place to false brethren?
options: To maintain truth of the gospel
questions.correctAnswer: To maintain truth of the gospel
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:5 explains that the truth of the gospel might continue with them.

questions.question: Who seemed to be somewhat in conference?
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:6 refers to those who seemed to be somewhat, implying false brethren.

questions.question: What did God accept according to Paul?
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:6 states that God accepteth no man's person.

questions.question: To whom was the gospel of the uncircumcision committed?
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:7 indicates that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed to Paul.

questions.question: The gospel of the circumcision was committed to whom?
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:7 states that the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter.

questions.question: True or False: Paul took Titus with him to Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:1 states that Paul took Titus with him to Jerusalem.

questions.question: True or False: Titus was a Jew.
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:3 describes Titus as being a Greek, implying he was not a Jew.

questions.question: True or False: Paul was compelled to be circumcised.
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:3 states that Titus, who was with Paul, was not compelled to be circumcised, and implies that Paul was not either.

questions.question: True or False: The truth of the gospel was compromised by false brethren.
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:5 indicates that Paul did not give place to false brethren for even an hour, emphasizing the truth of the gospel was maintained.

medium.title: Galatians Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Galatians Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who was perceived to be a pillar among the apostles according to Galatians 2:9?
questions.explanation: James, Cephas, and John were identified as pillars in Galatians 2:9, indicating their important leadership roles.

questions.question: What does Galatians 2:10 encourage believers to remember?
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:10 instructs that believers should remember the poor, which reflects the heart of Christian charity and concern.

questions.question: What was Paul's response when he saw Peter's behavior in Antioch?
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:11 states that Paul withstood Peter to the face because he was to be blamed for his actions.

questions.question: According to Galatians 2:12, why did Peter separate himself from the Gentiles?
options: He was commanded to do so
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:12 reveals that Peter withdrew from the Gentiles out of fear of those who were of the circumcision.

questions.question: How did Barnabas respond to Peter's dissimulation according to Galatians 2:13?
options: He was carried away with it
questions.correctAnswer: He was carried away with it
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:13 indicates that Barnabas was also carried away by the dissimulation of the other Jews.

questions.question: What is the main issue Paul addresses regarding Peter in Galatians 2:14?
questions.explanation: In Galatians 2:14, Paul points out that Peter's actions were not in accordance with the truth of the gospel, highlighting the need for integrity in belief and practice.

questions.question: According to Galatians 2:8, who was mighty in Paul towards the Gentiles?
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:8 states that the same God who worked effectively in Peter also worked in Paul toward the Gentiles.

questions.question: What does Galatians 2:5 emphasize about the truth of the gospel?
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:5 highlights the importance of maintaining the truth of the gospel without yielding to false pressures.

questions.question: What was the relationship between Paul and Barnabas as described in Galatians 2:1?
questions.explanation: In Galatians 2:1, Paul mentions going to Jerusalem with Barnabas, indicating their partnership in ministry.

questions.question: What does Galatians 2:7 reveal about the gospel commitment given to Paul?
options: It was the same as Peter's
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:7 shows that Paul was entrusted with the gospel of the uncircumcision, distinguishing his mission from that of Peter.

questions.question: What does Galatians 2:6 indicate about God's view on human status?
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:6 states that God does not show favoritism, emphasizing His impartiality in accepting people.

questions.question: According to Galatians 2:4, what was the concern regarding false brethren?
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:4 warns that false brethren came in to spy out the liberty believers have in Christ, which is a threat to the gospel's truth.

questions.question: True or False: Paul was hesitant to confront Peter about his behavior.
questions.explanation: Paul confronted Peter directly as stated in Galatians 2:11, indicating he was not hesitant to address the issue.

questions.question: True or False: The right hand of fellowship was given to Paul and Barnabas.
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:9 confirms that James, Cephas, and John extended the right hand of fellowship to Paul and Barnabas.

questions.question: True or False: Paul believed that all believers should be circumcised to be saved.
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:3 indicates that Titus, a Greek, was not compelled to be circumcised, affirming that faith, not circumcision, is the basis for salvation.

hard.title: Galatians Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Galatians Chapter 2.

questions.question: According to Galatians 2:15, who are described as 'Jews by nature'?
options: We who are Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles
Those who are circumcised by the law
questions.correctAnswer: We who are Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:15 explicitly states 'We who are Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles,' distinguishing Jews by birth from Gentile sinners.

questions.question: What is the basis for justification according to Galatians 2:16?
options: By the faith of Jesus Christ
By the works of the law
questions.correctAnswer: By the faith of Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:16 clarifies that justification is 'not by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ,' showing faith as the means of justification.

questions.question: In Galatians 2:17, how does Paul respond to the idea that Christ might be the minister of sin if believers are found sinners?
options: We must find a new way
We should return to the law
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:17 states 'God forbid,' rejecting the notion that Christ ministers sin even if believers are sinners while seeking justification by Him.

questions.question: What does Paul say about rebuilding what he destroyed in Galatians 2:18?
options: He follows the law more strictly
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:18 explains that rebuilding what was destroyed causes Paul to 'make myself a transgressor,' indicating disobedience to the gospel truth.

questions.question: According to Galatians 2:19, what is the relationship between Paul and the law?
options: Through the law, I am dead to the law
I am justified by the law
questions.correctAnswer: Through the law, I am dead to the law
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:19 states 'For I through the law am dead to the law,' meaning Paul has died to the law's authority through the law itself to live for God.

questions.question: In Galatians 2:20, Paul says, 'I am crucified with Christ.' What does he emphasize about his life after this crucifixion?
options: Christ lives in me, and I live by faith in the Son of God
I live by the law of Moses
I live by my own works
questions.correctAnswer: Christ lives in me, and I live by faith in the Son of God
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:20 expresses that though Paul lives, 'not I, but Christ liveth in me,' and his life is by faith in the Son of God who loved and gave Himself for him.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'dikaioō' in Galatians 2:16 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Dikaioō' in Galatians 2:16 means 'to justify or declare righteous,' referring to being made right before God through faith.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Galatians 2:20, where Paul contrasts 'I am crucified with Christ' and 'Christ lives in me'?
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:20 uses a chiasm structure by placing 'I am crucified with Christ' and 'Christ lives in me' in a mirrored contrast, emphasizing union with Christ.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of justification by faith found in Galatians 2:16?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:4 ('the just shall live by his faith') echoes the justification by faith theme that Paul emphasizes in Galatians 2:16.

questions.question: Galatians 2:21 states, 'If righteousness come by the law, then Christ is dead in vain.' Which New Testament passage echoes this teaching?
questions.explanation: Romans 3:28 teaches similarly that 'a man is justified by faith apart from the works of the law,' echoing Galatians 2:21 on the futility of law-based righteousness.

questions.question: What event immediately preceded Paul's confrontation with Peter at Antioch as recorded in Galatians 2:11?
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:12 notes that Peter ate with Gentiles before 'certain men came from James,' which led to his withdrawal and the subsequent confrontation in verse 11.

questions.question: How does Paul's statement in Galatians 2:19 reflect Old Testament typology?
options: It echoes the death to the law as a type of the old covenant passing away
It refers to the flood as a cleansing
It alludes to the Exodus as liberation
It describes the Day of Atonement rituals
questions.correctAnswer: It echoes the death to the law as a type of the old covenant passing away
questions.explanation: Paul's death to the law in Galatians 2:19 typologically reflects the passing away of the old covenant, fulfilling Jeremiah 31:31-34's promise of a new covenant.

questions.question: In Galatians 2:17, Paul asks if Christ is the minister of sin. What rhetorical device is he using here?
questions.explanation: Paul uses a rhetorical question in Galatians 2:17 to emphasize that Christ cannot be the minister of sin, underscoring the absurdity of the idea.

questions.question: True or False: According to Galatians 2:21, if righteousness is achieved by the law, Christ's death is rendered ineffective.
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:21 states, 'if righteousness come by the law, then Christ is dead in vain,' confirming that reliance on the law makes Christ's death ineffective.

questions.question: True or False: Galatians 2:20 teaches that Paul lives independently and not by faith in Jesus Christ.
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:20 says 'Christ liveth in me' and 'I live by the faith of the Son of God,' indicating Paul does not live independently but by faith in Christ.

theological.title: Galatians Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Galatians Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Galatians 2:16 teach about justification?
options: Justification is by faith in Jesus Christ, not by works of the law
Justification is based on adherence to the Mosaic law
Justification is achieved through ritual circumcision
Justification requires both faith and law equally
questions.correctAnswer: Justification is by faith in Jesus Christ, not by works of the law
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:16 teaches clearly that man is not justified by works of the law but by faith in Jesus Christ, emphasizing faith over law for justification.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christian liberty does Galatians 2:5 affirm?
options: The gospel's truth must not be compromised by legalistic bondage
Christian liberty allows believers to transgress the law
Liberty is a license to sin without consequence
The law should be observed fully to maintain gospel truth
questions.correctAnswer: The gospel's truth must not be compromised by legalistic bondage
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:5 emphasizes refusing to give place to false brethren who would bring believers into bondage, preserving the truth of the gospel.

questions.question: What doctrine about the unity of the gospel mission is taught in Galatians 2:9?
options: The apostles acknowledged distinct missions for Jews and Gentiles
Only Jewish believers are part of the gospel mission
Gentiles must first become Jews to be saved
The gospel mission is exclusively for the circumcised
questions.correctAnswer: The apostles acknowledged distinct missions for Jews and Gentiles
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:9 shows James, Cephas, and John giving fellowship to Paul and Barnabas, recognizing their mission to the Gentiles while they ministered to the circumcision.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Galatians 2:6 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:6 states that God accepts no man's person, demonstrating God's impartiality in accepting all without partiality.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is prominently shown in Galatians 2:20?
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:20 highlights the love of God who gave Himself for us, demonstrating divine love.

questions.question: How does Galatians 2:11–14 connect to the broader biblical theme of justification by faith over works?
options: It illustrates conflict over Gentile inclusion and the rejection of legalism
It endorses strict observance of Jewish customs for salvation
It advocates for the circumcision of all Gentile believers
It shows that Peter opposed the gospel of grace
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates conflict over Gentile inclusion and the rejection of legalism
questions.explanation: In Galatians 2:11–14 Paul opposes Peter’s withdrawal from Gentiles, affirming justification by faith and opposing Judaizing legalism.

questions.question: In what way does Galatians 2:1–2 prepare for the revelation of the gospel to the Gentiles in Acts?
options: By showing Paul’s private confirmation of the gospel to the apostles
By emphasizing the necessity of Gentile circumcision
By rejecting Gentile inclusion in the church
By advocating for a new law for Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: By showing Paul’s private confirmation of the gospel to the apostles
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:1–2 details Paul’s visit to Jerusalem to confirm the gospel he preaches to Gentiles, which anticipates the mission to Gentiles in Acts.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Galatians 2:19 and 2:20 teach about sanctification?
options: Believers are dead to the law and live by faith in Christ who lives in them
Sanctification is achieved through strict law observance
The law empowers believers to live righteously by their own strength
Christ’s indwelling is optional for sanctification
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are dead to the law and live by faith in Christ who lives in them
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:19-20 teaches that through the law believers die to it and live by faith in Christ, who indwells them for sanctification.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about gospel freedom is taught in Galatians 2:3 and 2:4?
options: Gentile believers are not compelled to be circumcised because false brethren try to impose bondage
All Gentiles must be circumcised to be saved
Circumcision is irrelevant to gospel freedom
False brethren encourage liberty from the law
questions.correctAnswer: Gentile believers are not compelled to be circumcised because false brethren try to impose bondage
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:3-4 explains Titus was not compelled to be circumcised despite pressure from false brethren seeking to impose legalistic bondage.

questions.question: What theological synthesis about apostolic authority and mission is taught by Galatians 2:7 and 2:8?
options: God empowered Peter for the circumcised and Paul for the Gentiles with equal authority
Peter had authority over all churches including Gentiles
Paul’s mission was subordinate to Peter’s
The apostles disagreed about mission priorities
questions.correctAnswer: God empowered Peter for the circumcised and Paul for the Gentiles with equal authority
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:7-8 shows God empowered Peter and Paul for distinct but equally authoritative missions to Jews and Gentiles respectively.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Galatians 2:17-18 suggests that seeking justification by Christ leads to sinning. What does this passage actually teach?
options: That Christ is not the minister of sin and rebuilding the law leads to transgression
That seeking justification by Christ encourages sin
That justification by Christ nullifies the need for righteousness
That all sin is excused because of faith
questions.correctAnswer: That Christ is not the minister of sin and rebuilding the law leads to transgression
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:17-18 refutes the idea that Christ encourages sin; it teaches that returning to the law after faith in Christ causes transgression.

questions.question: What doctrine about fellowship and unity is taught in Galatians 2:9?
options: The apostles recognized and affirmed differing ministries but maintained unity
Fellowship was restricted to Jewish believers only
Gentiles were excluded from apostolic fellowship
questions.correctAnswer: The apostles recognized and affirmed differing ministries but maintained unity
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:9 shows James, Cephas, and John gave fellowship to Paul and Barnabas, acknowledging distinct ministries yet maintaining unity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Galatians 2:21 manifest in relation to grace and law?
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:21 emphasizes not frustrating God's grace, reflecting God’s faithfulness in saving by grace, not law.

questions.question: What theological synthesis about the nature of human sin and justification is taught in Galatians 2:15 and 2:16?
options: Jews by nature are sinners and justified by faith apart from the law
Jews are righteous by nature and do not need faith
Justification requires works of the law regardless of nature
questions.correctAnswer: Jews by nature are sinners and justified by faith apart from the law
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:15-16 teaches even Jews by nature are sinners and must be justified by faith, not law works.

questions.question: How does Galatians 2:10 relate to the broader biblical theme of social justice and Christian responsibility?
options: Believers are urged to remember the poor as a vital part of Christian faithfulness
Christian faith is only about personal salvation, not social concerns
The law requires neglecting social duties
Remembering the poor is optional and not important
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are urged to remember the poor as a vital part of Christian faithfulness
questions.explanation: Galatians 2:10 shows that apostles required remembering the poor, linking gospel faith with social responsibility.
